7af7b8f73f0a.content: WoW.... is is an incredible and uplifting story. Apparently happened only 3 miles north on the Garden State Parkway from my exit. Happened in Aug.... but I have not heard of this till now. Everyday hero's. ... and yet another Hero Officer. New Jersey State Police Recently, we received this letter from a passing motorist who witnessed Trooper Jamarr Morris helping a little boy and his two dogs on the Garden State Parkway: I am writing this letter to inform you of an incident that took place on the southbound side of the New Jersey Garden State Parkway on Monday, August 23 at approximately 2:45 PM in the area of mile marker 112. I was driving home from work. I am a new commuter, and being so new I have become very cognizant of the deer that roam the side of the parkway no matter the time. I try to remain vigilant to their whereabouts, as I know they pose quite a threat of accident. On this particular day I noticed two dogs and their 8 year old owner running in tow in the woods where these deer typically feed. They were headed directly for the parkway. I had an immediate pit in my stomach! As both a mother and educator, I anticipated that if these dogs ran onto the GSP that the little boy would be quick to follow. And that is exactly what happened! I along with two other motorists slowed the traffic to a dead stop, I know...not the easiest decision to make, nor the best! But the crisis I foresaw was too grim to imagine any other way. Fortunately Officer Jamar Morris (car 204) was only about 1.5 miles ahead. I believe he was on a recent traffic stop. He must have noticed that the traffic was not moving and he safely turned his vehicle around and returned to the scene which included two loose dogs running all over the GSP, one 8 year old boy who seemed to be in shock who was chasing them, and 5 patient adults who had stopped the traffic and were trying their best to render aid. Officer Morris quickly and calmly took control of the scene. The young boy was able to only capture one dog. He only had one leash. Officer Morris grabbed the other dog and carried him. I am not sure he even liked dogs. He took the young man to the Trooper vehicle. I could hear him asking the young boy where he lived and what had happened. He scooped them all into the vehicle and safely moved over to the side of the road. The whole incident took less than 5 minutes. As Officer Morris passed my vehicle all I could say to him was "YOU ARE A HERO!" And maybe we were all heroes that day, right down to the little boy who just didn't want to lose his dogs. But this was Officer Morris's scene that day! He took charge of what could have been an incredible tragedy on the Garden State Parkway. That young boy and his pups all put their heads on the pillow safely that night, as did we all! Life never prepares us for these types of days! We all just lead with our hearts and calmness of mind! As I put my own head on the pillow on that Monday night I really wished I could have had a group hug and a moment with all these individuals. Thank you Trooper Morris, the concerned citizens that stopped to help, and the motorist who shared this story with us.

0e24c06f8780.content: DEPRESSION TIPS: Shower. Not a bath, a shower. Use water as hot or cold as you like. You don’t even need to wash. Just get in under the water and let it run over you for a while. Sit on the floor if you need to. Moisturize everything. Use whatever lotion you like. Unscented? Dollar store lotion? Fancy 48 hour lotion that makes you smell like a field of wildflowers? Use whatever you want, and use it all over your entire skin. Put on clean, comfortable clothes. Put on your favorite underwear. Those ridiculous boxers you bought last christmas with candy cane hearts on the butt? Put them on. Drink cold water. Use ice. If you want, add some mint or lemon for an extra boost. Clean something. Doesn’t have to be anything big. Organize one drawer of a desk. Wash five dirty dishes. Do a load of laundry. Scrub the bathroom sink. Blast music. Listen to something upbeat and dancey and loud, something that’s got lots of energy. Sing to it, dance to it, even if you suck at both. Make food. Don’t just grab a granola bar to munch. Take the time and make food. Even if it’s ramen. Add something special to it, like a soft boiled egg or some veggies. Prepare food, it tastes way better, and you’ll feel like you accomplished something. Make something. Write a short story or a poem, draw a picture, color a picture, fold origami, crochet or knit, sculpt something out of clay, anything artistic. Even if you don’t think you’re good at it. Create. Go outside. Take a walk. Sit in the grass. Look at the clouds. Smell flowers. Put your hands in the dirt and feel the soil against your skin. Call someone. Call a loved one, a friend, a family member, call a chat service if you have no one else to call. Talk to a stranger on the street. Have a conversation and listen to someone’s voice. If you can’t bring yourself to call, text or email or whatever, just have some social interaction with another person. Even if you don’t say much, listen to them. It helps. Cuddle your pets if you have them/can cuddle them. Take pictures of them. Talk to them. Tell them how you feel, about your favorite movie, a new game coming out, anything. May seem small or silly to some, but this list keeps people alive. *** At your absolute best you won’t be good enough for the wrong people. But at your worst, you’ll still be worth it to the right ones. Remember that. Keep holding on. *** In case nobody has told you today I love you and you are worth your weight and then some in gold, so be kind to yourself and most of all keep pushing on!!!! Find something to be grateful for! May I please get 2 friends or family members to copy and re-post? I am trying to demonstrate that someone is always listening. #SuicideAwareness #HaveARealConversation #988Lifeline #ificandoityoucandoit #speakupagainststigma #EndStigma Just two. Any two. Say done. Someone is happy because you exist ♥️

3bf7ed8b4cbc.content: This is the start of the "Kesselchen" at the 'Ring. I call it the "Kessel Run" and try to do it in less than 12 parsecs. If you round down. 😁 (Han Solo fans know what I'm talking about.) 🤣 It's kind of a backstraight -- if you look at the yellow dot on the track map of the 15-mile 'Ring -- except it's not straight at all. 🤦 It's a series of curves. Taken flat-out. Foot to the floor. 170-180mph. In the first picture, see the curve ahead? Flat-out. Picture 2? Flat-out. Picture 3? Foot nailed to the floor. 🤷🏻‍♂️ I especially like that corner because if you hit it just right, you arc beautifully through the next 180mph corner without moving the steering wheel. 🥱 Just a nice high-speed blast through the Eifel countryside. 🇩🇪

9d16f7ab7a80.content: Here it is! The Flügplatz. The Flying Place. The place on the 'Ring where cars in the olden days would take off, and land down the road. Like I'd said, better hope the tires were pointing in the right direction when you landed! ✈️ With the aerodynamic downforce on today's cars you don't get that drama. The pure racing Porsche 919 is GLUED to the road. The production-based Ferrari 296 GT3 feels a little light, a little unsettled, but ultimately just tracks straight. 🚂 Oh, btw. That turn up ahead? Taken flat-out. 🤣🤣🤣

e38f901eacb5.content: I love it when a plan comes together. The best I could do on the 13-mile Nürburgring Nordschleife Tourist circuit with the Porsche 919 hybrid was a 5:39. The record is 5:19, with that same car. 😲 To improve, I decided to turn continuous laps on the 15-mile Gesamtstrecke (Nürburgring Overall Circuit). With the Tourist, there's a start and a finish, and then you have to pull off and stop at the toll booth to go around again. 🤦🏻 First time on the Gesamtstrecke, I did 3 laps and was wasted. But I wanted to work on endurance and concentration, so I gradually built up the number of laps each time. 💪🏻 When I tried the Tourist today, I cut my personal best by SEVEN SECONDS!!! From that 5:39 down to 5:32. Not by working on speed but on concentration and endurance. Funny how that works. 😉

e7a98240d3d2.content: My next improvement program with sim racing is to feel and understand the cars better. I've been concentrating on learning the tracks, now I want to better understand the cars. 🔩 Today I drove some of the GT3 category cars at the Glen to compare their different characteristics. Drove the Lexus RC F, the Lamborghini Huracan, the BMW M4, and the Corvette. Tomorrow I'll do the rest: Mercedes, Aston Martin, Ferrari, Mustang, Porsche. 🔧 Kind of eye-opening. 😕 I hated the Corvette because I really had to work to get the front end to grip -- yet I did my fastest time with it. 🤣🤣🤣

fe9f7706df07.content: After Day 2 of comparing GT3 cars at Watkins Glen, I needed a muffuleto. And if you're like the various delis and sandwich shops I follow, you have to OVERDO it! 🤣 Unfortunately, on a wrap not crispy bread, but: pesto, olive salad, provolone, mortadello, capacolla, Genoa salami, ham, mozzarella, arugula, and a drizzle of balsamic vinegar. 😋 Now I won't need dinner...

329369e165b4.content: On Day 2 of my GT3 car comparison, I drove the Audi R8, the Aston Martin Vantage, and the Mercedes AMG GT. The Audi's handling was stable and benign. Did whatever I wanted it to do. ⚓ Right away I could feel the Aston was nose-heavy. The engine is in front of the driver, but set so far back in the chassis that it's considered a mid-engined car. 🏹 Still, I had to get that massive weight pointed in the right direction to get fast times. And it posted the fastest time of all so far. 🤷🏻 The Merc has that same chassis layout but seemed lighter, had quicker steering, and tended to wander if I didn't purposefully point it. I was 2 seconds slower with it than with all the other cars. ⏳ But this is the car multiple F1 World Champion, Max Verstappen, chooses to race and win with during his downtime. The takeaway? It's possible the other cars shield my weaknesses, and the Merc highlights them. 🤔

5b803260a038.content: I need this displayed every time I get into the sim rig! Thanks, guys! 🤣🤣🤣 Drove the last four GT3 cars: McLaren, Porsche, Mustang, Ferrari. I'm amazed again at how completely different these cars drive. But that's the idea. 💡 I've mostly worked on learning the different tracks: the 'Ring, Monza, Monaco, the Glen, Le Mans, Spa, etc.. And though I used a variety of cars, it was really about the tracks. 🤓 Now I've switched my focus to *feeling* the cars more -- trying to absorb their characteristics and find their limits. And eventually, feeling when they're at the limit *BEFORE* they go over the limit! 🤦🏻

Who's ahead in gymnastics rn? 🫠 What's difficult today isn't technological -- it's mental -- keeping track of the momentum in two-plus different sporting events simultaneously. But that just comes down to brain training. 😉

afba15b404ca.content: No, I'm not a private investigator checking up on a wayward spouse. On my way to and from my current job, I pass different restaurants, and it makes me think back to Friday lunches in the corporate world. 🤔 The huge facilities (1000+ people) I worked in always had an incredible cafeteria (or two, or three!), but come Friday, especially in good weather, we were *out the door* to nearby restaurants! 🚀 And Friday generally being a half day during the summer -- once we had a long, relaxed lunch with lots of camaraderie and laughter -- we stood talking in parking lots just like this. 🗣 Then we'd head home. Not the office. Hello, weekend!!!

90be6183225a.content: Eau Rouge. Radillion. The 6-hr WEC race at Spa-Franorchamps today. 🏁 Watched qualy yesterday to see how I stacked up against the world's leading endurance drivers. The Hypercars did a lap at just over 2 minutes. My best was a 2:11 in the Aston Martin Valkyrie hypercar. 🏁 I haven't used a GT3 car there, they were lapping at around 2:16. I did use a 2024 F1 car there and did a 1:57 -- besting even the hypercars -- but an F1 isn't designed to race for 6+ hours.

69a3e92cb9c5.content: Last day of the GT3 comparison at the Glen. Had to do the Ferrari, Lambo, Corvette, and Porsche for the second time. Great, but also frustrating! 🤷🏻 With the Ferrari, I got down to 1:48 -- seemingly without trying! Then the Corvette, which I'd had trouble with last week, I got down to a 1:49!!! Last week, 1:50 was the best I could do with any of the 11 cars, with most in the 1:51, 1:52 ballpark. 👍🏻💪🏻 So I was excited, but with the Lambo, I struggled. 1:52. And the Porsche, 1:53! Wtf? But I may have been tired. The important thing is that I tried all 11 GT3 cars twice, got to know their different characteristics, and drove them in anger. 😠 The real GT3 record at the Glen is 1:44. The sim record is 1:42. (Ideal track conditions, no wind, etc....) 🏁

675bf6b00a35.content: Then there was that time I worked for the non-profit trying to get a bill passed by the NJ legislature that would help low-income households with their utility bills. 📉 Can't remember the name of the non-profit. It was based in Irvington, and we would arrive in the early evening to learn which town we would canvas that night for signatures on the petition. From Bergen down to Middlesex counties. 🚙 One night in New Brunswick, a man wanted to hear more. Invited me in to sit, and then grilled me on the proposed bill. 🤔 I think my concern and naivete must have impressed him. He signed. 👍🏻😁 (Don't try to decipher my handwriting. No one can read it. 🤣🤣🤣)

8eb464395b88.content: Beer! What's that? 😁 🍻 After a hot Summer's day in Spring -- slaving over a hot uhd tv and watching ND MLAX win against JHU -- what better way to relax than a cold beer? 🍺 These and some Dogfish Head beers are finally going to be consumed this year! I think the DF brews are two years old. Think they're chilled by now? 🤣 When I think back to the glory days of the craft beer revolution! Tried so many different types of beers. And there were so many different ones to try! But it expanded my palate. Which I now appreciate. 👍🏻

598e889b021e.content: I think of it as a controlled crash. At Monaco -- among the glitterati -- the guardrails are always just centimeters away, the curbs are willing to pitch the car into the guardrails if you even look at them wrong, and the car is exploding around a too-narrow, constantly undulating public road surface. 🎢 I hate the place. 😠 Yet today, I lowered my personal best NINE seconds to a 1:33 in the F2 car. 😳 It's because of all the other hard work I've done over the last few months on all the other different race circuits with all the different types of race cars. It translates. 🏋🏻‍♂️ But it IS kinda neat to blast through one section, just barely keep the car under control and not hitting anything, and then blasting on to the next section. In the millisecond I have to reflect, I think, "That was kinda fun." 😊 I still hate the place. 🤣

b7f78ab4316d.content: I love when these bushes by the front door come to life in the Spring. But what I like more this particular Spring is our new occupants starting to come to life, and starting to claim this place as their own. Their homes. 👥 We've had a rash of new people moving in over the past few years, and it's interesting to see the dynamics. Apparently, they're all very respectful and respectable. 😁 They've been deferring to the "long-time occupants" in terms of the parking spaces nearest the buildings. 😔 Until recently. 😶 I've always encouraged them that there's no assigned parking, but they continued to defer and park way in the back of the lot. 🫡 So, good to see them today FINALLY make this place their own. Finally taking the parking spots closest to their building without a second thought! As if they LIVED here!!! 🤣🤣🤣 Because they do. 😉

ee0f8409493f.content: Happy start to the Memorial Day weekend! You need to decide how you want your dogs this weekend! 🤣 Oh, and stay warm! And dry... 😕

5807cc7badf6.content: This is the ~40mph chicane at Monza -- at the end of the almost 200mph, flat-out front straight. 🚀 And after months, and miles away at other circuits, but coming back to this circuit a fair amount, I finally have a "pretty good" braking point to slow down enough for this corner. Efficiently. ⚓ It's actually too conservative, but it's infinitely better than where I was before! I need to cut things closer. But that will come with time, visualization, and muscle memory. 💪🏼👍🏻

06dd2b1817c7.content: It was a cold day much like this that I first appeared on ESPN. 🤣 Broadcasting the F1 race at Montreal, they did a long crowd shot of the hairpin stands. Everyone bundled up in warm outerwear. Except... 📺 Me. They pulled the shot closer to show me in my shorts and white t-shirt in this sea of multi-colored parkas. I'm totally unfazed by the cold, clammy weather. 😊 I'd worn a parka also, with the shorts, but as we were packed together like sardines in the stands, I was overheating and took off the parka. 😰 Anyone who knows me knows I generally wear shorts from April to November. I have a VHS of that race somewhere, or maybe I can find the vintage broadcast on YouTube? Take a screenshot? 📱

ca863e4f6f5c.content: Happy Memorial Day to all! Remembering all who paid the ultimate price in service to our country. 🫡 Rainy here this weekend, and my marigold barrier is loving it! Keeping the animals away from what will hopefully be cilantro, oregano, and rosemary. We'll see if anything comes up. 🤷🏻‍♂️

0501e9358353.content: So it's New Jersey-style Italian dogs this holiday! The Chicago-style was excellent, but gotta try different dogs. 🌭 Angus beef hot dog, boardwalk-seasoned hash browns, basil, oregano, ketchup, yellow lantern sauce instead of mustard, peppers, onions. Kind of a Jimmy Buffs, right? 🌭

afa5da0974b3.content: I tell ya... nothing's going right, you hang your head, figuring tomorrow's another day. And then you shave 11 whole seconds off one of your personal bests. 🤣🤣🤣 Did La Sarthe today with the BMW Hyper Car. The car that hasn't done much until it recently won the endurance race at Spa, and finished 2nd this past weekend at Detroit! Two diametrically opposed circuits! 🥵 Couldn't get it to do sh**. It hates braking while cornering, and it tended to plow -- which scrubs off speed. So I'm having a frustrating day. 😕 I jump over to the Nürburgring Gesamtstrecke with the Mercedes AMG GT3 to clean the palate. This is the car I struggled with at the Glen. 😮 I'm sloppy. Transitioning from the Hyper Car to the slower, less-responsive GT3 isn't going well, but I relax and figure I'll just get some laps under my belt. Look up at the end, and I shaved ELEVEN SECONDS off my PB with the Merc! What dafuq??? 🤣🤣🤣

a0542246e650.content: I told you about the Monaco GP's twisting, undulating circuit. Monaco is built on the side of a mountain. So it's those up-hill-down-dale kind of public roads that the race course uses. ⌛ After concentrating on Monaco recently -- I don't hate it anymore. I've come to look at the track the way I'd look at moguls on a ski slope. ⛷️ Because the circuit constantly undulates, I've been looking for the best places -- the rise in a corner, a pavement change before a corner, a mid-straight bump -- to apply throttle, steering, brake. Work off of the moguls. 🧑🏻‍🩰 I have to read the pavement better. Most race circuits are smooth as glass. Not this one!

b13479d1eb82.content: With the 24 Hueres du Mans this weekend, here are the Practice 1 times for the Hyper Car group. The fastest cars are in the 3:26 range. ⏱️ My fastest time -- ever, at La Sarthe-- was a 3:29 in the "no rules" Porsche 919 Evo. My best in a Hyper Car is 3:36 -- so, 10 seconds slower than the pros. 🤷🏻‍♂️ But I'm using a software model generalized for the Assetto Corsa (sim race software) community. If I played around with the gearing, say, for more top speed... and used super soft tires... adjusted the brake bias... maybe... 🤔 (Chart copyright FIA/WEC)

ee0f24a9742f.content: You have to hear a train whistle while out watching minor league baseball. Have to have a train whistle. The MLB? You hear jets overhead from the major airport. ✈️ With these games, you're in the stands sitting back because there's not a big crowd. One team is up 1-0, but nothing -- really -- has happened yet. Everybody's waiting to see if anything does. 🚂 Then the train whistle blows. Since time immemorial that's been minor league ball. ⚾ For the local Somerset Patriots, the tracks are right before the Raritan River, so you hear the nearby clickety-clack, too. Sit back, and wait. 🍿

63435dce1a34.content: It's 9:56 PM @ Le Mans and pretty much everybody is still going strong. Great weather. No rain. Yet.😉 😎 Love watching the in-car views, but the directors never hold the scene long enough. I want to see where they brake, turn in. Where they hit the apex. The directors cut to the outside view. 🫤 I've driven there so much on the race sim, I know every corner by heart. I was busy this week and didn't do ANY sim racing! Surprising, I know! 🤣 Next week. 🏎️

467d66890a24.content: My outdoor lotus pond. Actually, there're two, but the other was the original, and I may have used too big of a dose of mosquito dunk, which may have inhibited plant growth. 🦟 The lotus has always figured prominently in my life. As a kid, I followed the Lotus race cars in F1 because founder Colin Chapman was such an innovator. With my discovery of Eastern religions in H.S., the lotus was central in their belief systems. 🪷 After college, when I was an aspiring (amateur) musician, John McLaughlin's Mahavishnu Orchestra had a jazz song I loved, "A Lotus on Irish Streams"... 🕉️ Might as well try to raise me some lotus plants! 😁 😉

99fca1db71be.content: Summer smoothies. Or, the first attempt: mango nectar, lime juice, tomatoes, carrots, ginger slices, fresh basil from the garden, and the omnipresent, omnipotent roasted dandelion root tea. 🍋‍🟩 I think it needs more lime. I drink lime or lemon water throughout the day, so maybe that's why I want a higher concentration here. 🤷🏻

e83f0a0903e4.content: Back after 2 weeks off visiting family and friends and relaxing. Getting away from the sim. 😎 That was a good thing. 😁 Sometimes, you need to digest, and you can only do that if you take time to let your body do what it needs to do. A siesta, perhaps. 🛌 So, I didn't turn any great times this week, but everything felt more comfortable. Natural. A lot of racing is visualization and muscle memory -- same as any sport, really. The second you use your brain, you're screwed. 🛟 Just let your body -- your being -- do what you've trained it to do. That's how you succeed. Can't wait until next week. 🏎

d5cefdf05e50.content: One thing about the World Cup -- well actually, a huge thing about the World Cup is the unbelievably rabid fans! 🍻 The huge contingent of Scottish fans practically drinking Boston dry! The Aussie fans chanting in the streets of Seattle: "Aussie boys are on a bender, Donald Trump is a sex offender!" 🤷🏻 But it's all good fun -- for now. (And on the other TV I have the New Hampshire Fisher Cats versus the Binghamton Rumble Ponies. Don't you love the AA ball club names?) ⚾

71fa6c4b42e4.content: What I like about the World Cup, and about soccer in general is that there are white guys with man buns. Like mine. 😁 There're none in MLB. Some in the NBA, but not really the white guys. A lot of long hair in the NFL, but a bun interferes with the helmet. NASCAR? They just rediscovered mullets. ✂️ When I had my hair trimmed yesterday, I told the stylist not to touch the length. Told her I was watching the World Cup, and some of the guys had longer tails hanging out their man buns -- which I had previously disliked. 😞 But that I now wanted to be like the cool kids. So I could look like them and sit at their lunch table. 😉🤣

80ab04db488c.content: Though I was very excited to get back to sim racing yesterday, I was perhaps more excited to be driving by the store that carries the big bottle of the Tabasco Scorpion Pepper hot sauce! 🤣🤣🤣 Tabasco is famous for their eponymous hot sauce, but they kinda got left behind in the battle of HUGELY HOT hot sauces. Not. Any. More!!! 🚀 Instead of paying $10-$25 for the unbelievably, unbearably, exceptionally hot niche sauces, I can now get Tabasco's kick-ass (where's the milk???) scorpion sauce for only 3.89!!! 😳 My hot sauce adventure naturally started with Tabasco, then I moved to Jamaican Choice. JC had some hotter sauces -- and more exotic flavors. So, I want to try this one to see where it fits in my culinary universe. 📡

dc3b115ae7e5.content: So, I'm back. After taking time off to enjoy family and friends, then coming back to the sim -- I kinda struggled. As I figured, though, I just needed to get the rust out. 🧹 Today at Monza I shaved THREE WHOLE seconds off my PB with the 2026 F1 car!!! I've been working religiously on the 3 chicanes: Turn 1, Lesmo, and Ascari. They're starting to flow. 🕺 Then to Brands! Clean the palate at the end of the day, and have some fun on the tiny up-and-down course. 🛝 Lowered my PB by 2 seconds. Finally learning my craft. 😁

5cf82b08299a.content: It's a muffuletta world, we just live in it -- until hot dog and hamburger season comes along. 🌭🍔 Came back to the delish muffulettas, only with a twist: the handmade olive salad now features tomato slices to sharpen things up! 🍅 So, green olives, black olives, onion, garlic, cooked peppers, not-sundried tomatoes -- all piled onto the meats and cheeses in a dense wrap. 🌯 Seasoned with arugula, pesto, balsamic, dried oregano, fresh basil from the garden. Heat all to the same, mild warmth... 🌡️ Yum. (Though I should be eating more dense protein for the weightlifting I'm starting again... after muffuletta season...)

1dd8f00e0fd2.content: SVG qualified on pole. Love qualified further back. And Conor Zilisch qualified WAY BACK. But, huh, how about that? They're all now up front! The guys that love the road courses. 🤔 During the pre-race, I started thinking about how I'd drive the course. I've never been on it in the sim. But preternaturally I start debugging it, and so will have to try it on the sim. 🤣 Meanwhile, the sports car guys are qualifying at the Glen. And England is up over Panama in the WC in New York, New Jersey. Wherever that is. 😉

ab408b4353be.content: The Cross Still Offends By Pastor Rich Bitterman The bullet tore the air in half. A folding chair rattled. A Bible dropped. A young man slumped sideways beneath a white event tent, eyes wide with the weight of eternity. It was supposed to be a conversation. A “prove me wrong” segment. But this time, rebuttal came not with words, but with a rifle. Charlie Kirk didn’t get to finish his sentence. I got the news just before prayer meeting. I contemplated this death as I prepared to lead the saints in prayer. But I didn’t feel like praying. Not tonight. My hands were still. My mouth was ready. But my soul was pacing. Angry. Grieving. Tempted. Tempted to grow quiet. Tempted to sit this one out. Tempted to wonder if any of this, faith, boldness, public gospel witness, is still worth it. Because hatred in this country isn’t simmering anymore. It is boiling. Europe is trembling. Israel is burning. Rockets lit the sky over Gaza again. And now, here on American soil, the blood of a Christian apologist paints the pavement of a university quad. What do you do with that? What do you say when courage gets gunned down in daylight? Charlie Kirk was no perfect man. None of us are. But he had backbone where most of us don’t anymore. He was a believer. Unashamed. Unafraid. He understood that real conversations only happen when truth is welcome at the table. And the truth he carried most was Christ. He brought the gospel into public space on purpose. Because the gospel isn’t supposed to stay in church basements and private Bible studies. It is meant to confront. It is supposed to offend. It was not made for safety. The Word became flesh and they nailed Him to a tree. So of course they came for Charlie. Of course they reached for a gun. This is what evil does when it runs out of arguments. It doesn’t reason. It kills. That’s the part that catches in my throat. Not just the sadness, but the strategy of hell behind it. The Enemy wants us afraid. He wants us to see what happened to Charlie and backpedal. He wants the rest of us to whisper, to soften the message, to believe the lie that faith should stay private. But Christ never whispered. He preached in temples, on hillsides, in courtrooms, at dinner tables. And when they told Him to be quiet, He picked up His cross. Not a symbolic one. A real one. Heavy. Bloody. Splintered. When Jesus said, “Follow Me,” He didn’t hand out maps. He handed out crosses. That’s what I remembered tonight. I sat in our prayer space, surrounded by saints who had brought prayer lists and worn Bibles. And I realized I didn’t want to lead them in mourning. I wanted to lead them into battle. Not with banners or fists, but with open Bibles and tear-stained prayers. The kind of war that kneels in gravel beside the wounded, hands them living water, and refuses to leave. The kind that speaks both mercy and judgment without flinching. The kind Charlie died for. This world is not a friend to grace. But grace isn’t fragile. “Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?” Paul didn’t leave that question unanswered. “Shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword?” —Romans 8:35 He piles up every fear you and I carry and then sets them on fire. “No. In all these things we are more than conquerors.” That means bullets don’t win. Slander doesn’t win. Prison bars don’t win. Death doesn’t win. You can lose everything in this world and still walk into glory with your head lifted high. Because the love of God in Christ Jesus isn’t suspended by headlines or gunfire. There are two worlds unfolding right now. The one you see. And the one you don’t. One is filled with chaos. The other is filled with crowns. I believe that when Charlie Kirk’s body slumped to the concrete, his soul stood upright in heaven. Not limping. Not silenced. Not stunned. But crowned. He didn’t fall. He crossed. The great cloud of witnesses gained another voice. And I wonder if Stephen met him there. The first martyr. The man who got stoned for preaching what the crowd didn’t want to hear. The man who, in his final breath, saw the heavens open. The only time in all of Scripture we see Jesus standing at the right hand of God, rising to receive one of His own. I like to believe He stood again. Are you afraid? Do you feel the tremble in your spirit? Do you wonder if it’s still worth it to speak boldly, to carry your Bible, to preach the gospel in a world that doesn’t just disagree but wants you gone? You’re not alone. You’re not weak for feeling that. But you are called to something stronger than silence. Don’t let fear become your theology. The cost is high. But the reward? The reward is Christ. And He’s not a concept. He’s a King. Heaven is not empty. It is filled with scarred saints who refused to bow to fear. Men who were stoned. Women who were burned. Children who sang while the flames climbed. And every last one of them arrived. There is no difficulty that can cancel the promise of God. There is no persecution that can derail your destination. There is no sniper’s bullet that can separate a soul from Christ. Your life is not measured by how long you live on earth, but by how much of it was spent pointing to heaven. Paul said, “I have fought the good fight… I have kept the faith.” Then he looked toward the reward. Not a monument. Not a mention in history books. But a crown. Handed to him by the One with nail marks still in His hands. So let me say this clearly. We do not mourn like the world mourns. We do not write eulogies dripping with sentiment. We sing songs of resurrection. We carry the banner of a Kingdom that does not tremble. Charlie Kirk did not die for nothing. He died carrying the same message you and I must now carry forward. The cross stands tall. The tomb is still empty. And the gospel has not lost one ounce of power. So pick up your cross. Wipe your eyes. And keep going. The crown is worth it. The King is coming. And there’s still time to speak. Even if they shoot. Lord, give us courage. And if not safety, give us joy. For we carry not just the message, but the marks. And You are worth every bruise, Faith & Values !!!! The hateful evil ones killed Charlie Kirk ! But they will not win! It’s sickening how some of these young people are cheering his murder! Frankly shocking to hear all this hate! Parents need to teach their children faith and values! How else will they grow up to be responsible adults? God save us from these evil ones ✝️

9d02168aedf4.content: D-Day was the name given to the June 6, 1944, invasion of the beaches at Normandy in northern France by troops from the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom and other countries during World War II. France at the time was occupied by the armies of Nazi Germany, and the amphibious assault—codenamed Operation Overlord—landed some 156,000 Allied soldiers on the beaches of Normandy by the end of the day. Despite their success, some 4,000 Allied troops were killed by German soldiers defending the beaches. At the time, the D-Day invasion was the largest naval, air and land operation in history, and within a few days about 326,000 troops, more than 50,000 vehicles and some 100,000 tons of equipment had landed. By August 1944, all of northern France had been liberated, and in spring of 1945 the Allies had defeated the Germans. Historians often refer to D-Day as the beginning of the end of World War II.

Let’s break it down, because I’m tired of being told what I believe and what I stand for. Spoiler: not every conservative is the same, but most of us I know share these same principles. 1. I believe America should stay out of endless foreign conflicts. We are not the world’s sugar daddy, and we shouldn’t act like it. 4. I believe no foreign aid should be given until every veteran at home is taken care of. 5. I believe immigrants make America stronger — when they come legally. I’m a conservative because I believe in faith, family, freedom, and personal responsibility. I don’t want a government that controls every aspect of our lives - I want a government that protects our rights, secures our borders, defends our freedoms, and then gets out of the way. We are strongest when Americans take care of America first, when families are supported, when our veterans are honored, and when our children are given truth, not propaganda. The fox was first reported acting sick near Brushwood Point along Hartshorne Road in the Rumson and Navesink section. Last Thursday, park rangers located the carcass inside Hartshorne Woods Park and turned it over to Middletown Animal Control. The animal was sent to a state lab for testing. Results came back positive Tuesday. Officials are reminding residents not to approach or handle wildlife and to make sure all pets are up to date on rabies vaccinations. Animals should not be allowed to roam off leash, even in wooded areas, to avoid contact with potentially infected wildlife. Rabies is a fatal disease that spreads through bites or contact with saliva. If you see a sick or injured animal, call Middletown Animal Control at 732-615-2097 or contact police after hours at 732-615-2100. Anyone who may have been exposed should seek medical attention immediately. Pet owners should contact a veterinarian if their animal had contact with wildlife.

The sheriff’s office shared an image of an alligator in a law enforcement uniform receiving an award. A man accused of running from law enforcement by cutting through a swamp on Sunday was soon greeted by something potentially scarier than jail time: an alligator. Even more worrying for him, the giant lizard was not too keen on him getting away either. Big picture view: The 40-year-old man, who was wanted by Louisiana State Police, entered the swamp after St. Charles Parish Sheriff’s Office deputies saw him walking along a highway, the Sheriff’s Office explained in a post. Once in there, he was greeted by an alligator that attacked him and injured both of the man’s arms. The suspect managed to escape the alligator on the ground, but he could not get away from the drone in the sky, the Sheriff’s Office continued. A drone team with the Sheriff’s Office spotted him and alerted deputies, who took him into custody. He was taken to a nearby hospital and is expected to be booked into the St. Charles Parish jail. What they're saying: When noting the suspect’s ill-advised detour through the swamp, the Sheriff’s Office wrote, "An alligator joined the law enforcement team and tried to convince [the suspect] that surrendering was the better option, but he thought otherwise." The post from the Sheriff’s Office included a pair of photos showing an alligator wearing a law enforcement uniform and, in one of them, it was being presented with an award. The St. Charles Parish Sheriff's Office shared this photo of an alligator wearing a law enforcement uniform in a post about the arrest of a DWI suspect. (St. Charles Parish Sheriff's Office) The backstory: The chase for the suspect began after Louisiana State Police troopers were alerted to a reckless driver on Interstate 10, according to the Sheriff’s Office, which also cited reports that the driver had struck a concrete barrier and blown a tire. After troopers located the driver and stopped him on Interstate 310, they determined that he was showing signs of impairment. While troopers were investigating the man for a DWI, he jumped off the elevated roadway and went into the swamp, the report added. He was later seen by deputies walking along another highway and then ducked back into the swamp. That’s when he met the scales of justice. What's next: The suspect is expected to be booked on counts of operating a vehicle while impaired and resisting an officer. The alligator was not hurt in the confrontation, the Sheriff’s Office noted, while adding one last reminder.
